full_judgment:
2. The predecessor of the opposite parties Md Abdul Khayer Chowdhury, as plaintiff, has filed another class suit being No.358/78 in the 2nd Court of the Munsif, Rangpur, for declaration of his title to the suit land stating, inter alia, that the disputed land belonged to Wakf Estate of Bhangni Mosque and one Munirunessa Chowdhury made wakf of the suit property along with other property in favour of the said Bhangni Mosque in the year 1287 BS. Munirunnessa remained as Mutoalli of the wakf property during her life and after her death one Enayet Karim Chowdhyry became Mutoalli of the said property of the Mosque. Enayet Karim as Mutoalli of the Mosque appointed Abul Khayer Chowdhury as Moazzin of the Mosque and gave him the suit land in the year 1287 BS to enjoy the same in lieu of his service as Moazzin, Abul Khayer Chowdhury rendered his service as Moazzin and grew crops, created house on plot No.676 and the suit land was recorded in CS Khatian in his name as Chakran for the purpose of giving Azan in the Mosque. When the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into force, the suit land was recorded in the name of Abul Khayer Chowdhury as tenant. Since then Abul ''Khayer Chowdhury has been possessing the suit land till his death. But during life time of Abul Khayer Chowdhury defendant No.1 the present petitioner, the Mutoalli of the Wakf Estate, directed Abul Khayer Chowdhury to surrender the possession of the suit land on 24-9-78. Then he filed the suit for declaration of his title to the suit land, During pendency of the suit Abul Khayer Chowdhury died and his heirs have duly been substituted as plaintiffs. Defendant No.1 the Mutoalli of the Wakf Estate, contested the suit by filing a written statement wherein he stated that previous Mutoalli Enayet Karim Chowdhury, never granted lease of the suit land to Abul Khayer Chowdhury permanently and he appointed Abul Khayer Chowdhury as Moazzin of the Mosque on condition that so long he would discharge his duties properly, he would be entitled to enjoy the suit land as Moazzin and that he would have no right to hold the land after giving up his service or on ceasing to perform his duties, Abul Khayer Chowdhury managed to prepare the record of rights of the suit land in his name and against which the defendant filed an appeal and the said appeal was allowed and the record of right of the suit land was corrected accordingly. Abul Khayer created some collusive sale deeds in respect of the suit land in favour of one Bachcha Mia and his son Abul Ali Chowdhury. Since Abul Khayer Chowdhury did not surrender the possession of the suit land the present Mutoalli applied for his eviction and the same is pending before the Administrator of Wakfs. Abul Khayer Chowdhury ceased to perform his duty since more than 20 years and he had no tenancy right to the suit land, so the suit is liable to be dismissed. The learned Munsif considering the evidences on record decreed the suit. The petitioner then preferred the appeal before the learned District Judge and the said appeal was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge who by his judgment and decree dated 28-5-86 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the trial court''s Judgment. Being aggrieved at and dissatisfied with the above decision the petitioner preferred this application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure to set aside the impugned judgment and decree. 

 3. Mr Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submitted that the suit land was made wakf in favour of the mosque and, as such, "Allah" becomes the owner of the suit property and the Mutoalli of the Wakf Estate is only a caretaker of the land and he has got no right to settle the land permanently to any person on behalf of Allah and that Allah is not a juristic person according to section 3(39) of the General Clauses Act or rent receiver according to section 2(23) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act-1950 and, as such, section 11 of the said Tenancy Act will not apply in this case. It is admitted that the suit land is a portion of land of Wakf property of Bhangni Mosque and Enayet Karim was the Mutoalli of the said Mosque. It is also admitted that the suit land was given to Abul Khayer Chowdhury for service as Moazzin of Bhangni Mosque and the same was recorded in the CS Khatian as Chakran for giving azan of the Mosque. So the suit land was given to Abul Khayer in lieu of his service of Bhangni Mosque. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that for giving service as Moazzin no one can claim salary according to Muslim law. He referred to Hedaya page 499 translated in English wherein it is stated that First the Prophet has said, read the Quran but do not receive any recompense for so doing, and also directed Oathman Bin Abaseeyes that if he were appointed a Moazzin (a cryer to prayer) he should not take any wages. Accordingly, to that view a Moazzin is not entitled to salary in any way. But the Motualli of the Mosque had given the suit land to Abul Khair for performing his duties that is, for giving Azan, of Bhangi Mosque on condition that when he ceased to give Azan of the Said Mosque he will not be entitled to use the land for cultivation or any other purpose. The said case was given to him for a particular purpose of the Mosque and it has not been settled to him permanently by the then Mutoalli to perform Azan of the Mosque by him and after his death by his heirs or by his nominee. The owner of the property is Bhangni Mosque which is permanent. The land of the Wakf Estate is guided by the Wakf Ordinance. There is no evidence on record that Mutoalli had taken permission from Administrator of the Wakfs to give the suit land to Abul Khayer for his service to the Mosque. There is nothing on record that there is any condition in the wakf deed that the Mutoalli can give land of the Mosque to any person for his service to the Mosque, Against the above submission the learned Advocate for the opposite party Mr. Akram Hossain Amin submitted that Abul Khayer Chowdhury has acquired occupancy right in the suit land after promulgation of EBSA and T Act and according to section 11 of the said Act he is not a tenant under the Government in the land and his name has duly been recorded and that since the suit land was recorded as Chakran Land in the CS Khatian and he continued his tenancy right of said land after promulgation of the EBSA & T Act, 1951 and has been continuously possessing the same, he acquired valid title to the land. The Courts below decreed the plaintiffs title to the suit land taking the view that the same was chakran land of Abul Khayer and, as such, he became tenant according to section 11 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In the Wakf property the owner of which is a Mosque and the Mosque will continue according to Muslim law up to "Day of Judgment "and service of it will continue up to that day. The Chakran land as defined in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is for the person is rent receiver or subordinate rent receiver. After acquisition of interest of such rent receiver the land given to the servant by the rent receiver is liable to be kept by those servants and the same is inheritable as the service of servant is not required by the rent receiver after acquisition of their Estates. But service of the Mosque will continue till Dooms day as it is stated above. In the evidence on record it is found that the Bhangni Mosque is still in existence and the service of the said Mosque Moazzin of giving "Azan" of the said Mosque is continuing and same will continue. In that view of the matter the Chakran land given for Azan of the Mosque cannot be considered as equal to the Chakran land as stated in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. So, the view taken by the court below can not be considered as correct view in respect of the land of Wakf State. Considering this view I find no substance in the submission made by the learned advocate for the opposite party. Since the Wakf land which is given to Allah for the purpose of His House, the Mosque, the said land cannot be alienated by anybody or even by Mutoalli unless condition is laid down in the Wakf deed by the maker. It has already been said that no such condition is found in the record and, as such, it cannot be said that Abul Khair or his heirs can acquire any right to the property without performing the specific duty "Azan" to the Mosque, So in view of the above discussion I find substance in the application. The court: below erred in law in deciding the suit.
